samples.summary: `--quiet` is no longer an output-suppression control, so command result bodies (document content, file listings, api-key material) are now written to stdout even when the operator explicitly asked for silence
samples.evidence: Before this change `output(data, fmt, quiet)` early-returned when `--quiet` was set, and every command site passed `opts.quiet`; `api-keys create` had to opt out explicitly (`output(res.data, opts.format, false)` — old packages/cli/src/commands/api-keys.ts:20) precisely because the raw key is sensitive. After the change `output()` takes no gate at all (packages/cli/src/output/formatter.ts:26) and unconditionally `console.log`s the body. Attack/exposure path: an operator or CI job that ran `wafflebase docs content <id> --quiet` (or `files list --quiet`, `api-keys list --quiet`) to avoid dumping workspace data into a shared build log now gets the full body in that log; the only remaining way to suppress it is `>/dev/null`, which is not documented in the updated README/`docs/design/cli.md` §9 text. The change is intentional and documented for the *body-is-data* reason, but the removed behaviour was also the only in-CLI control over what confidential document content reaches captured stdout, and neither doc hunk tells users that.

samples.summary: Moving stdin/`--data` JSON.parse inside the try makes V8's parse-error message (which quotes a slice of the input) reach stderr unconditionally, echoing secrets from the payload even under `--quiet`
samples.evidence: `cells = JSON.parse(dataStr)` / `JSON.parse(Buffer.concat(chunks)…)` (packages/cli/src/commands/cells.ts:117-124) is now inside the try, and the catch calls `outputError(e)` (line 146), which after this change always prints `error.message` to stderr (packages/cli/src/output/formatter.ts:52-57) — the old `outputError(e, quiet)` returned silently under `--quiet`. Modern V8 JSON parse errors embed a ~30-char excerpt of the offending input (e.g. `Unexpected token 'x', "{\"token\":\"wfb_…" is not valid JSON`). So `wafflebase sheets cells batch doc-1 --data '<malformed JSON containing a credential>' --quiet`, or the same payload piped on stdin, now writes part of that payload into the CI/stderr log. Impact is bounded (the caller supplied the data), but the envelope is emitted with no redaction of the echoed input.

samples.summary: `output()` writes server-controlled strings to the terminal unescaped in `table`/`csv` formats, so control/ANSI sequences in attacker-chosen document titles are re-emitted verbatim — now on the `--quiet` path too
samples.evidence: `output()` does `console.log(format(data, fmt))` with no sanitisation (packages/cli/src/output/formatter.ts:26-28); for `--format table|csv` the payload is raw server data (document `title`, cell values) rather than JSON-escaped text, unlike `outputError`, whose `JSON.stringify` escapes control characters. A user sharing a workspace who names a document with an embedded ESC sequence can drive the reviewer's/agent's terminal (cursor moves, clearing prior output, OSC sequences) when they run `wafflebase docs list --format table`. Pre-existing in `format()`, but this change adds a new reachable path (the `--quiet` case, exercised by the new test at packages/cli/test/output.test.ts asserting `docs list --quiet --format csv` prints the body).

samples.summary: Command arguments touched by this change (`docId`, `tabId`, `sref`) are interpolated into request paths without `encodeURIComponent`, allowing client-side URL path traversal out of the workspace-scoped base URL
samples.evidence: `getCells`/`getCell`/`setCell`/`deleteCell`/`batchCells` build `${this.base}/documents/${docId}/tabs/${tabId}/cells/${sref}` with no encoding (packages/cli/src/client/http-client.ts:334-356; same for `getDocument`/`updateDocument`/`deleteDocument` at 198-206), while `downloadFileDocument` does encode (line 254). WHATWG URL normalises `..` segments before fetch, so a value such as `wafflebase sheets cells get '../../<other-ws-id>/documents/x' A1` (reached via the diff's packages/cli/src/commands/cells.ts:23-25) sends the caller's Authorization header to an arbitrary path on the configured server, escaping the `/api/v1/workspaces/<ws>` prefix the CLI believes it is pinned to. This is a real concern for the documented agent-driven usage, where the doc id can come from untrusted content. Impact is limited to the caller's own privileges because `WorkspaceScopeGuard` re-checks membership/key scope server-side (packages/backend/src/api/v1/workspace-scope.guard.ts:26-35), so it is not an auth bypass — but the client-side scoping is not enforcing anything. Pre-existing code, not added by this diff.
